Fixed in `app.py`: a bad `day` now gets a 400 with a JSON error message instead of a 500 and a traceback. I called the app directly with both dates from your access log plus a few others; there's no test suite in the project, so that was the only check.

| Request | Response |
|---|---|
| `day=2026-09-31` | 400 `invalid day '2026-09-31': no such date (day is out of range for month)` |
| `day=14/09/2026` | 400 `invalid day '14/09/2026': expected a date as YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `day=2026-13-01` | 400 `invalid day '2026-13-01': no such date (month must be in 1..12)` |
| `day=` or no `day` at all | 400 `missing 'day' parameter: expected a date as YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `day=2026-09-13` | 200, same summary as before |

The missing/empty `day` case was also a 500 before, so I covered it too.

The check accepts exactly what `trips.py` accepts, so valid requests behave as before. That means a few non-dashed ISO forms such as `day=20260914` still return 200, as they did before. If you want strictly `YYYY-MM-DD`, that's a one-line tightening — say so and I'll add it.

The date picker is still sending these bad values; this change only makes the API answer them properly.
